speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific triggers for your gait instability, such as worsening symptoms in the dark or after drinking alcohol? Also, could you describe exactly where you feel the most significant ataxia, in your legs, arms, or both?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of appearing drunk and right-sided clumsiness is concerning. Has your vision changed, particularly regarding your ability to track moving objects or see clearly in dim light? Additionally, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
